provenance: Opus 5.5 subscription CLI draft with host review/repairs, source restrictions and execution verification.

draft_notes.explanation:
The mechanism is unchanged. A periodic texture is wiped to palette[0]. The largest rectangle sets the canvas. Every later rectangle is nested in the D4-mapped image of the original bottom-left corner of its container. A frame's container is its interior; a solid's container is its full area. A filled frame becomes a frame plus an inner block that exactly fills it, which reproduces the generator's j-offset.

Texture detection is repaired:
- A colour is texture if it has more than 4 four-connected components, or its bounding box is only 1 cell thick. Every object is at least 2x2.
- Then a fixed-point pass reclassifies as texture any remaining colour whose bounding-box ring shows a known texture colour. For colours that are not ring-shaped, the whole box is checked instead. This is sound because object pixels can only be overwritten by later objects, never by texture.

Why 4 is the right bound:
- Any later rectangle is smaller than an earlier frame in both dimensions, so it meets that frame's ring in a single arc.
- A later hollow frame removes two pieces of that arc, because its interior leaves the earlier ring visible.
- With at most 4 objects, a ring therefore splits into at most 4 pieces.
- A rectangle minus one smaller rectangle stays connected, so solids are one piece.

The corner mapping, frame/solid discrimination and placement code are kept from the previous candidate. The constructor proposal only adds rejection of one genuinely ambiguous random configuration. Fixtures, the API and the mechanism are unchanged.
draft_notes.limitations:
No tests have been run.

The texture test can still fail if heavy occlusion leaves a texture colour with 4 or fewer visible vertical runs. For that to happen, the colour must also never appear in a 1-thick bounding box or inside the ring or box of a candidate object. This seems extremely rare in the generator's domain, but it is not proven impossible.

Without the proposed constructor repair, the solid-over-solid-interior ambiguity remains. It occurs when a solid of at least 5x5 is followed by a solid of exactly (w-2)x(t-2) placed precisely over its interior. The program reads this as a filled frame.

The constructor repair slightly lowers the frequency of two-solid scenes in that one exact configuration. Its rejection loop has the same open-ended structure as the original sampler, and the rejection probability is tiny.

The frame check uses the generator's 5x5 minimum frame size. Area ties do not occur in the generator; if one did, it is broken deterministically by larger minimum side, then colour.
draft_notes.diagnosis:
The failed factory classified any colour with more than 3 components as texture. Its justification was that each later object cuts a frame ring at most once. That is false for a later hollow frame: its top and bottom edges both cross the earlier ring, and its hollow interior leaves the ring visible between them.

In counterexample pair 2 (d4=0), the outer frame (visible colour 1, 15x11) is split into exactly 4 pieces:
- the solid block 7 cuts its top edge;
- the hollow frame 6 crosses its right side twice, at rows 2 and 9;
- the solid block 2 cuts its left side.

The program therefore discarded colour 1 as texture. It then used the 6 frame as the canvas, so the output had the wrong size and contents.

With the bound restored to 4 pieces, as in the archived solver, the trace for this pair is: frame 1 becomes the 11x15 canvas; frame 6 goes at rows 2-9, cols 1-12; solid 7 at rows 4-8, cols 2-9; solid 2 at rows 5-8, cols 2-8. That matches the expected label. The other three pairs already passed, and their classification is not affected by this change.
draft_notes.constructor_issue: No constructor change. Host reproduced that solid-inside-solid candidates already return None because every filled interior must remain visible; proposed extra rejection was redundant.
draft_notes.host_review: Constructor change rejected: the proposed solid-inside-solid ambiguity is already rejected by draw(), which requires every solid interior cell to retain its own colour. Keep the original generator. Apply four-fragment classification and iterative texture exclusion; fresh validation pending.
draft_notes.rejected_cli_constructor_claim:
Constructor defect (needs host review): when num_solid=2, the second solid can be exactly (w-2)x(t-2) and placed at (r+1, c+1) on a first solid of at least 5x5.
- That input is pixel-identical to a filled frame (outer = first colour, inner = second colour).
- The generator's outputs differ for the two readings, because a filled frame increments j and two solids do not.
- No visible rule can separate them.

The proposed constructor rejects that configuration in random sampling only, so the filled-frame reading becomes the unique one. The fixtures do not contain this configuration and are unchanged. The displayed counterexample is not a constructor error; it was a factory bug.
